# Incident Report — Host Compromise via Information-Stealer Malware

**Case:** mta-2022-01-07 | **Evidence:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` + `exported_objects/` | **Capture window:** 2022-01-07 20:04:09 → 20:16:39 (approx.)

## 1. Victim Host Identification

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **192.168.1.216** | DHCP, NBNS, ARP, all traffic |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** | ARP (192.168.1.216 ↔ 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), matches DHCP client-id `01:9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9` |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** | DHCP option 12 hostname (hex-decoded: `4445534b544f502d47584d594e4f32` = "DESKTOP-GXMYNO2"); NBNS shows the same host as `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2` / `SPOONWATCH` |
| AD domain | spoonwatch.net (DC: SPOONWATCH-DC, 192.168.1.2) | DHCP option 15, DNS SRV lookups, Kerberos/LDAP traffic |
| Logged-in Windows user | **steve.smith** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 192.168.1.216 and the DC (192.168.1.2) |

## 2. Malware Family and Attribution

**Assessed family: Vidar Stealer (or a very close Arkei/Raccoon-lineage fork).**

**Attribution basis: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence set — only the pcap and carved HTTP objects — so there is no signature hit to cite. The call is based on the following observed behavior, which matches this stealer family's well-documented modus operandi:

- The infected host opens a single persistent HTTP connection to `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP stream 65, port 49738→80) at **20:07:32**, contacted directly by IP with **no preceding DNS lookup** — consistent with a hardcoded C2 IP.
- It issues six sequential `POST /osk//N.jpg` requests (N = 1–7, skipping `6.jpg` which returns an empty MIME boundary). The server's "jpg" responses are not images — they are legitimate third-party Windows DLLs:
  - `1.jpg` → `sqlite3.dll`
  - `2.jpg` → `freebl3.dll` / `nss3.dll` (Mozilla NSS libraries)
  - `4.jpg` → `msvcp140.dll` / `vcruntime140.dll` / `concrt140.dll`
  - `7.jpg` → `vcruntime140.dll` (API-set stubs)
  - `3.jpg`, `5.jpg` → additional supporting DLLs/API-set stubs
  
  Fetching the NSS/SQLite library set disguised with image extensions is the signature technique Vidar (and its Arkei/Raccoon relatives) uses to read Firefox/Thunderbird's encrypted credential/cookie stores on a fresh victim.
- The host then check-in's with `POST /osk//main.php`.
- Finally, it exfiltrates a single archive, **`_5861695120.zip`** (379,485 bytes), via `POST /osk/`. The zip's central directory lists:
  - `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`
  - `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`
  - `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`
  - `outlook.txt`
  - `passwords.txt`
  - `screenshot.jpg`
  - `system.txt`

  This `autofill / cc / cookies / outlook.txt / passwords.txt / screenshot.jpg / system.txt` folder/file layout is the canonical Vidar/Raccoon-style stealer log structure (browser autofill, saved cards, cookies, saved passwords, a desktop screenshot, and a system-fingerprint file).
- HTTP request headers on every request to the C2 carry `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`, a distinctive fixed header set commonly hardcoded into this stealer family's HTTP client.

No AV/EDR alert, YARA match, or file-hash reputation lookup was available to confirm this against a public signature database (and no internet lookups were performed per instructions), so treat the family name as a high-confidence behavioral assessment, not a confirmed detection.

The pcap capture does not contain the initial infection/delivery vector (dropper download, phishing email, exploit) — traffic in the capture begins with the host already authenticating to the domain controller, and the stealer's C2 beacon starts almost immediately (~3.5 minutes into the capture) with no observed dropper download preceding it.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control endpoint:**
- `2.56.57.108:80/tcp` (HTTP) — contacted by hardcoded IP, no DNS resolution observed
- No malicious domain observed; C2 was accessed by raw IP only

**Malicious URLs (all on 2.56.57.108, single TCP session, port 49738):**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (check-in)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (exfiltration POST endpoint)

**Transferred files and SHA-256 hashes** (carved from the pcap's HTTP objects):

| File (as transferred) | Direction | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `1.jpg` (sqlite3.dll, PE32 DLL) | C2 → victim | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| `2.jpg` (freebl3/nss3.dll, PE32 DLL) | C2 → victim | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| `3.jpg` (PE32 DLL) | C2 → victim | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| `4.jpg` (msvcp140/vcruntime140, PE32 DLL) | C2 → victim | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| `5.jpg` (PE32 DLL) | C2 → victim | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| `7.jpg` (vcruntime140/api-ms-win-crt, PE32 DLL) | C2 → victim | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |
| `_5861695120.zip` (stolen-data archive: autofill/cc/cookies/outlook/passwords/screenshot/system) | victim → C2 (exfiltration) | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` (as carved from the pcap's HTTP object export; note: the multipart re-assembly is partially corrupted downstream of the DEFLATE stream, which prevented full decompression of individual archive members — file listing and sizes above come from the intact ZIP central directory) |

**Not an indicator — verified benign:** the `am_delta_patch_*.exe` and `.cab` files pulled from `download.windowsupdate.com` / `au.download.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.225/23.38.189.201) are legitimate Windows Defender antimalware definition updates, retrieved over the standard `Windows-Update-Agent`/`Microsoft-Delivery-Optimization` user agents. All other external TLS/HTTPS destinations (bing.com, msn.com, *.microsoft.com, *.windows.com ranges) are routine Windows telemetry/update traffic and show no signs of compromise.

## 4. Summary

Host **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9)**, logged in as domain user **spoonwatch\steve.smith**, is actively communicating with C2 **2.56.57.108:80** running a stealer consistent with the **Vidar/Raccoon family** (behavioral attribution). The malware pulled legitimate NSS/SQLite/VC-runtime DLLs disguised as `.jpg` files to enable browser-credential-store parsing, then harvested autofill data, saved credit-card entries, cookies, Outlook data, saved passwords, a desktop screenshot, and system fingerprint info into `_5861695120.zip` and exfiltrated it to the same C2 over HTTP. Recommend immediate host isolation, credential reset for `steve.smith` and any accounts/cards captured by autofill or saved-password stores on this machine, and outbound blocking of `2.56.57.108`.
